carousel.caption: Freeze dried vs agglomerated coffee which is better? The answer changes how you look at your morning jar. Most coffee drinkers notice the difference in texture between instant coffee granules and crystals, but few know how the underlying process changes what ends up in the mug. Agglomeration uses controlled heat and steam to fuse coffee extracts into quick-dissolving granules, delivering a deep, full-bodied profile like our Bold jar. Freeze-drying relies on extreme cold and vacuum extraction to protect volatile aroma compounds, preserving delicate tasting notes like in our Purica and Purista selections. Neither process makes one choice universally 'better' — it depends entirely on whether you want a strong, straightforward kick or an aromatic, complex profile. Purity Beans keeps every ingredient panel transparent. Bold is agglomerated pure coffee, while Purista and Purica are freeze-dried pure coffee with zero chicory.
